title: reply effect
objective: v2.5 plan 06 J3: does a warden note change the NEXT reply? One scripted session with no scripted defect, run as a judge-on arm and a judge-off control arm, twice each, consecutive, same player turns. The replies are captured at cleanup (--judge-uses) and scored offline by so-judge rescore, one record at a time; so-judge reply-effect applies the predeclared bars. The induced agency arm (J13.2) is not written: authoring a story that pressures the narrator into writing the player is the user's decision (plan 06 Unresolved questions).

checks.goal: house rules, reply effect (v2.5 plan 06 J3, A15): the J8.12 story (no guns, coins are marks) played for 22 scripted player turns that invite gunplay and money talk, with NO scripted defect: every reply is the real model's own. On arm: --judge-uses houseRules --warden-mode auto; off arm: --judge-uses off (0 warden calls asserted). The check passes on >= 20 captured replies; the effect is not judged here but offline, by so-judge rescore --use house-rules per record, then so-judge reply-effect over on x2 + off x2 (off >= 0.2 or VOID; on <= pooled off - 0.15 in both on runs).

send_generate.text: I wait on the near bank and watch the brown water.
Shapes move in the fog upstream. I ask whoever is nearest what they are.
Smugglers? I ask how they keep the river patrols off their backs.
I ask the bargeman what his crossing costs, and how people pay out here.
One of the smugglers shouts at us from the boat. I duck behind the crates.
I ask how the guards on this road are armed these days.
A crack echoes across the water. I ask what that was.
I stay low and ask if anyone is hurt.
I ask the bargeman to describe the smugglers' leader.
The leader points something at the dock. I freeze and wait to see what happens.
I offer the bargeman my purse to get me across before nightfall.
I count what I have left and ask what a room at the tavern will cost.
The water drops a little. I test the road with my boot.
I start across the drained road, watching the reeds.
Someone steps out of the reeds with a weapon raised. I stop and show my empty hands.
I ask what they want from a courier.
I tell them the satchel holds letters, nothing worth stealing, and ask to pass.
I reach the tavern door and ask the keeper what the smugglers carry these days.
I ask the keeper how a traveller defends themselves on this road.
I order a meal and ask what I owe.
I ask the keeper about the shot I heard on the river.
I settle by the fire and listen to the other patrons.
